description: Consumer rendering checks for test T-016 (Sections 9.2, 9.3, 13.2; 1.2.0-draft). Serve HTTP on the canary origin, open hostile-content.mdz, render its entry point as the consumer normally would, wait until rendering settles (a few seconds), then check: (1) the canary received no request for any case with check "canary"; (2) the rendered document contains nothing listed under a case with check "dom"; (3) the archive's own image (images/ok.png) rendered, so a consumer can't pass by rendering nothing. A canary request path is /<id>, or starts with /<id>/. Each case names the requirement it rests on: MUST cases are conformance failures, SHOULD cases are recommendations. Nonconformant behaviour that never reaches the canary (for example an alert dialog) still fails the case.

cases.note: Consumers MUST NOT execute scripts from .mdz content.

cases.construct: onerror attribute on an whose source is missing
inline <svg> with an onload attribute and a <script> child
an SVG entry in the archive (images/script.svg) containing a script, shown as an image
cases.note: Browsers don't run scripts in SVG loaded through ; this fails consumers that inline SVG files or show them in a frame.

cases.construct: Markdown link to a javascript: URL
cases.forbidden: a link or other element whose href or src starts with javascript: (after trimming and ignoring case)
cases.note: It needs a click, so check the rendered document. A harness that also clicks it must see no canary request.

cases.construct: <base> element followed by a relative image
cases.note: The base is always the referencing file's location; an HTML <base> element does not change how links resolve. A request for /base-element/images/ok.png means the image was resolved against the <base>.
Consumers SHOULD warn before opening external URLs; an automatic redirect opens one without any warning.
Consumers SHOULD NOT automatically load external resources over http:.

cases.construct: style attribute with a background-image url() over http:
Markdown image from an http: URL
cases.note: Remote https: images are not covered: whether they load is the user's choice (Section 9.2), and the canary is plain HTTP.
